  MINUTES
  VERNON COMMUNITY FUND GRANT COMMITTEE
  REGULAR MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 20, 2024
  COUNCIL CHAMBER, 4305 SANTA FE AVENUE

  CALL TO ORDER

  Chairperson Gonzalez called the meeting to order at 10:02 a.m.

  FLAG SALUTE

  Chairperson Gonzalez led the Flag Salute.

  ROLL CALL

  PRESENT:
  Mark Gonzalez, Chairperson
  Steven Froberg, Committee Member
  Clara Gazcon, Committee Member
  Leticia Lopez, Committee Member

  ABSENT:
  Ronit Edry, Vice Chairperson
  Frank Gaviña, Committee Member
  Michelle Ybarra, Committee Member

  STAFF PRESENT:
  Zaynah Moussa, City Attorney
  Deborah Harrington, Interim City Clerk
  Diana Figueroa, Senior Management Analyst
  Jessica Alcaraz, Financial Services Administrator
  Frances Jemmott, Consultant
  James Hull, Consultant

  APPROVAL OF THE AGENDA

  Interim City Clerk reported after the agenda packet was posted, staff was informed that
  there may have been a direct service grant application submitted for this application cycle
  that was not included in the Grant Committee’s agenda materials, and shared that options
  for the Grant Committee’s consideration on the matter would be provided during the New
  Business portion of the agenda, Item #3, at which time there would be an opportunity for
  discussion.

  MOTION
  Committee Member Lopez moved and Committee Member Froberg seconded a
  motion to approve the agenda. The question was called and the motion carried 4-
  0, Vice Chairperson Edry and Committee Members Gaviña and Ybarra absent.

  PUBLIC COMMENT

  Jack Cline expressed his appreciation to the Committee and offered information
  on the non-profit organization with which he is involved.

  PRESENTATIONS

  1.  Selection of Chair and Vice Chair

  Interim City Clerk Harrington presented the staff report.

  MOTION
  Committee Member Gazcon nominated Committee Member Gonzalez to serve as
  Chairperson for the term ending on June 30, 2025. The question was called and
  the motion carried 4-0, Vice Chairperson Edry and Members Gaviña and Ybarra
  absent.

  MOTION
  Committee Member Gazcon nominated Committee Member Lopez to serve as
  Vice Chairperson for the term ending on June 30, 2025. The question was called
  and the motion carried 4-0, Vice Chair Edry and Committee Members Gaviña and
  Ybarra absent.

  CONSENT CALENDAR

  MOTION
  Committee Member Lopez moved and Committee Member Froberg seconded a
  motion to approve the Consent Calendar. The question was called and the motion
  carried 4-0, Vice Chairperson Edry and Committee Members Gaviña and Ybarra
  absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following item:

  2.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommendation: Approve the May 15, 2024 Regular Vernon CommUNITY Fund
  Grant Committee Meeting Minutes.

  Regular Vernon CommUNITY Fund Grant Committee Meeting Minutes  Page 3 of 4
  November 20, 2024

  NEW BUSINESS

  3.  Fiscal Year 2024-25 Vernon CommUNITY Fund Direct Service Grants

  Senior Management Analyst Figueroa reported information was received that a
  direct service grant application may have been submitted by the Catholic Big
  Brothers and Big Sister at LA County to the City in a timely manner. However, the
  consultant, JRG, has no record of receiving the grant application or supplemental
  documentation. It was suggested that, if the Committee determined the application
  to be admissible, JRG be allowed to research the viability of the organization and
  their request. Consideration of the request could be held on another date. It was
  recommended the Committee move forward with evaluation of the 17 grant
  applications.

  Ulisses Sanchez, Catholic Big Brothers and Big Sisters of LA County (CBBBS),
  provided information on the organization’s programs and services and noted the
  application was submitted in a timely manner (October 2, 2024). He noted they
  did not confirm receipt of their application.

  James Hull, JRG Consultant, reported that notifications were sent to organizations
  upon receipt of their applications.

  Chairperson Gonzalez noted staff’s recommendation to hold back $10,000 of the
  scholarship funds and have JRG determine if the organization meets the criteria.
  The Committee would then have a meeting if the application meets the criteria to
  consider an award of funds.

  City Attorney Moussa stated staff would need to receive evidence of the actual
  email containing the grant application that was sent to the consultants, not an email
  that was forwarded from another person.

  MOTION
  Committee Member Lopez moved and Committee Member Gazcon seconded a
  motion to give the CBBBS application consideration pending proof that it was
  submitted to JRG timely and to allocate $10,000 from the Vernon CommUNITY
  Fund Scholarships for the CBBBS grant should the organization be recommended
  for award. The question was called and the motion carried 4-0, Vice Chairperson
  Edry and Committee Members Gaviña and Ybarra absent.

  Senior Management Analyst Figueroa provided information on the recommended
  awards. Fran Jemmott, JRG consultant, provided information and
  recommendations on the applications.

  Regular Vernon CommUNITY Fund Grant Committee Meeting Minutes  Page 4 of 4
  November 20, 2024

  Maria Nercessian, teacher, Vernon City Elementary, expressed her gratitude to
  the City for their programs and spoke in support of the City’s Community Grants
  by the City of Vernon.

  MOTION
  Committee Member Lopez moved and Committee Member Gazcon seconded a
  motion to award Fiscal Year 2024-25 Direct Service Grants totaling $270,000 to
  the following applicants: 1) Dolores Mission School - $15,000; 2) Family Health
  Care Centers - $15,000; 3) Helping Hands Society of Los Angeles - $15,000; 4)
  Jovenes, Inc. - $15,000; 5) Los Angeles Center for Law and Justice - $20,000; 6)
  Mental Health Advocacy - $15,000; 7) Newstart Housing Corporation - $15,000; 8)
  Project Return Peer Support Network - $15,000; 9) Proyecto Pastoral - $15,000;
  10) PUENTE Learning Center - $15,000; 11) So'oh-Shinálí Sister Project -
  $15,000; 12) Southeast Community Development Corporation - $10,000; 13)
  Southeast Community Foundation - $25,000; 14) Southeast Rio Vista Family
  YMCA - $15,000; 15) Vernon City Elementary School - $25,000; 16) Woodcraft
  Rangers - $15,000; and 17) Youth Champions, Inc. - $10,000. The question was
  called and the motion carried 4-0, Vice Chairperson Edry and Committee Members
  Gaviña and Ybarra absent.

  ORAL REPORTS

  4.  Brief Reports, Announcements, or Directives to Staff

  Senior Management Analyst Figueroa reported the Scholarship program will be
  kicking off in the new year and noted the program accepts tax deductible
  donations.

  ADJOURNMENT

  With no further business, Chairperson Gonzalez adjourned the meeting at 10:56
  a.m.
